verdict.rationale: Svelte's own docs say .svelte.js/.svelte.ts files let you share reactive state across your app using built-in runes ($state, $state.raw, $derived, $effect), with no library needed. A community user independently confirms that Svelte's built-in Stores and Context system work well for sharing state. Missing for 10: detailed first-party documentation of global-state patterns (stores and context APIs are evidenced only by community comment), and explicit guidance on handling global state in SSR or multi-request scenarios.
